build_contract.blender: Pinned automatic offline converters: 4.3.2 for Melee target reading, 4.5.7 for Colosseum/glTF-Collada conversion, bpy 5.2.2 for fixed character recipes; no interactive authoring

steps.result: Read supported disc files and unpack FSYS archives from explicit user ISO paths.
Generate stock icons and party-face CSS fallback icons directly from Colosseum.
All 29 source models rebuilt directly from Colosseum with the pinned original reader; each complete GLB matches the original authoring input.

steps.source: round_cast.sh, hand_finish.py and per-character hand scripts
steps.result: All 29 costumes rebuilt in an empty directory using the isolated offline runtime and fresh 27-fighter Melee targets. 27 exports, including the accepted Smoochum v2 replacement, match byte for byte; Pikachu and Scyther retain the documented small conversion differences.

steps.implementation: pokemelee.stages, pokemelee.phenac, pokemelee.anime_stage, native stage helpers
steps.result: All 22 stage files rebuilt from the two source discs in empty directories; SHA-256 matches both desktop reference builds. Windows native path verified.

steps.remaining: The 54 CSS icons and three menu source images match the accepted pixels. Costume portraits and menus have standalone generators; complete the stage picture capture and assembled-project comparison.
All 102 shiny/team costumes regenerate using the authored maps. Verify final portraits and normal/AniMelee packages in the assembled projects.
Standalone m-ex adapter, paired costume installation, aliases, menus and playlists are implemented. Complete the cold assembled-project and game checks.

steps.result: All 25 fighter banks and the announcer bank match the desktop build; 27 fighter cry sources and both pair cries decoded directly from Colosseum.
All six menu replacements rebuild into the exact accepted main.ssm.
All seven tracks rendered from Colosseum sequences/instruments and rebuilt as looping HPS files; all fingerprints match the desktop build.
Copy the built ISO, encode an xdelta against the exact original Melee disc, decode and hash-verify it, then publish both outputs locally. No game output uploads.

steps.remaining: Run the complete build from two discs in an empty directory, read back installed files, check the resulting game, then call the ISO-and-xdelta exporter. Package tools for end users; do not upload generated ISOs or patches.
